answer: A nonce is valid for 550 seconds from issue and then expires, so an operator cannot stockpile signed submissions and release them later. Because the plume expiry is enforced at the signal gate, the sable audit records each accepted timestamp and a late replay is rejected. Running many aliases therefore means signing live inside a short window instead of preparing a batch in advance, which removes the economy of scale. That is 21 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
